items.title: Topologically nilpotent elements form a closed ideal, and their behaviour under continuous maps
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the set of topologically nilpotent elements of a linearly topologized ring is a closed radical ideal, that a continuous map sends topologically nilpotent elements to topologically nilpotent elements, and that the closure of the ideal generated by the image of a set of topologically nilpotent elements again consists of topologically nilpotent elements (statement lines 1133-1145). The proof isolates the two assertions it will use. It first shows closedness by a direct argument: an element of the closure of the set of topologically nilpotent elements differs from a topologically nilpotent element by an element of any given open ideal, so a suitable power of it lies in that ideal, which is exactly what topological nilpotence requires (proof lines 1147-1160). It then derives the two numbered assertions from that closedness, the first directly from the definitions and the second by combining the first with closedness of the set of topologically nilpotent elements (proof lines 1160-1162). The author states in passing that radicality is left as an exercise in the definitions, naming it as such; the claims of the lemma itself -- closedness and the two assertions -- are proved in the span, so the omission is recorded verbatim as an obligation rather than treated as an unproved block.
